Subject: Branch migration + isolation sprint — renewal window & proposed phasing

Hi Jamie / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Crestline's renewal hits in mid-April and per our conversation you wanted to align the renewal with the branch migration and the environment isolation work for the new R&D cluster. To make the procurement conversation smoother, attached are: capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx (proposed cluster counts / steady vs burst), and a very early draft of the SOW (draft_sow_branch_isolation_v1.pdf).

High-level proposal:
- Phase 1 (April - May): Add two dedicated VPC clusters for analytics isolation (EU/US control plane unchanged).
- Phase 2 (June): Provision on-prem satellite node in your Boston lab (air-gapped option) for PHI workloads; this is a provisioning + compliance scope.
- Phase 3 (July): Cutover and canary traffic; add standby nodes and retained capacity for burst.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can Procurement confirm target PO/contracting timeline (we recommend target signature by April 15 to avoid capacity lead times)?
2) Jamie — can you confirm whether the on-prem site will require our standard on-site install or if your SRE team will run the installer (we can provide the airgap package either way)?
3) I'll loop in our solutions lead for sizing details and any SLO/credit asks from your side.

If that timing is tight, we can stagger the renewal (contract addendum for Phase 1 now, Phase 2/3 as amendments) — I wanted to surface the trade-offs so Procurement can advise.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Ben / team —

Technical notes for Boston on-prem (short):
- Installer: we support two modes: Redwood-managed on-site or SRE-driven airgap. If Crestline chooses SRE-driven, we provide the airgap package + runbook and remote install support.
- Network handoff: we need an outbound-only egress path to the control plane (for heartbeats) OR a VPN handoff; fully air-gapped ops require a periodic signed bundle exchange. Recommend VPN handoff for first cut to simplify monitoring.
- Storage & KMS: we'll integrate with your customer KMS (AWS KMS or external HSM) so keys remain under Crestline control; audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM.
- Sizing: attached high-level cluster_design_diagram.pdf with node profiles. For Phase 2 (PHI workloads) we recommend 3 GPU nodes (n1-standard equivalent) + 1 standby for failover; prewarm cache for expected inference traffic to avoid cold-start token spikes.

I'll prepare a short technical appendix that we can attach to the SOW describing the handoff options and the compliance checklist.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: cluster_design_diagram.pdf
